text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Decision may delay mine: Newfoundland tells native people to negotiate own deal for share in Voisey's Bay.
- Chechen candidate eyes world approval: Independence election issue.
- Homeless man found frozen in garage: Medical officer to review cold-weather alert for getting people into shelters.
- Liberals' credibility dropping, poll finds: Promises questioned, CBC lobby says.
- Experts hope grafts can perpetuate tree: Golden Spruce unites Indians, loggers.
- Anglers brave danger to stay out on ice: After rescue of 300 from Lake Simcoe, enthusiasts want to retrieve their vehicles.
- Budget may bring tax breaks: Ottawa weighs partial exemptions of capital gains tax to encourage donations to charity.
- K mart fights for survival: Some skeptics fear discounter may be losing the battle.
- Silicon Graphics high on Octane: New computer touted as leader.
- Property stocks may cool off, analysts say.
- Morrison may seek rescue in royalty trust.
- Couche-Tard abandons C$68-million bid for Silcorp.
